title: Understanding N-gram Limitations
text: N-grams are useful for capturing sequences, but they can also capture unintended patterns. Consider how DNA sequences are structured and how N-grams might misinterpret these structures.

title: Non-Consecutive Segments
text: Think about how N-grams might mistakenly identify non-consecutive segments as meaningful sequences. How might this affect the interpretation of DNA sequences?

title: Meaningless Segments
text: Consider the significance of segments with fewer than $$3$$ letters in DNA. Why might capturing these as 'words' be problematic?

title: Overlapping Segments
text: N-grams can capture overlapping sequences. How might this lead to incorrect interpretations of DNA sequences?

title: Evaluating N-gram Strategy
text: Evaluate the statement: 'Segments of non-consecutive letters would be included, meaning ATGCA could suggest the word AGA.' Is this a valid concern for using N-grams in DNA sequences?

title: Assessing Meaningless Segments
text: Evaluate the statement: 'Segments with $$1$$ or $$2$$ letters have no meaning, which N-gram would capture as "words".' Is this a valid concern for using N-grams in DNA sequences?

title: Understanding Overlapping Segments
text: Evaluate the statement: 'Overlapping segments would be included, meaning ATGCA is broken up into $$3$$ overlapping words.' Is this a valid concern for using N-grams in DNA sequences?
